How numbers are passed to your texting app

Apple doesn't let Android phones join an iMessage group (the blue-bubble kind). No app can change that.

What does work is a group text (MMS, or RCS on iOS 18 and later) that iPhones and Androids can all reply to. GroupBridge sets that up for you:

1. Add everyone in the group: phone numbers, Gmail, iCloud and other emails. Type them, pick them from Contacts, or paste a list.

2. "Start group text" opens your texting app with every phone number filled in. Send a message and the group exists.

3. "Ask an iPhone member to add me" writes a message to someone in the iMessage group, telling them how to start a new group with you in it.

4. People in the group by email only can't get group texts. iCloud addresses work only in iMessage. Use "Email the group" to reach them, or ask them for their phone number.

Tip: in your texting app's settings, turn on group messaging (MMS) so replies go to everyone.
